cards.definition: large or important enough to have an effect
cards.example: There was a significant increase in car ownership after 2010.
Fuel prices rose; consequently, people drove less.
Some sectors grew, notably renewable energy.
A substantial proportion of graduates work abroad.

cards.definition: basic or hidden cause of something
cards.example: The underlying cause of the trend was economic growth.
I was over the moon when I passed the exam.
I eat fast food once in a blue moon.
I need to hit the books before the test.
The Reading test was a piece of cake for me.

cards.word: to be on the same page
cards.example: After the meeting we were all on the same page.

cards.definition: to increase at a constant, moderate rate
cards.example: Sales rose steadily throughout the decade.

cards.definition: to fall very suddenly and steeply
cards.example: Attendance plummeted after the ticket price doubled.

cards.definition: to stop rising or falling and stay constant
cards.example: Unemployment levelled off at around 6% after 2015.

cards.definition: to reach the highest point before declining
cards.example: Production peaked at 40,000 units in 2008.
Oil prices fluctuated wildly during the period.
There was a marginal increase in rural populations.
Spain and Italy accounted for 12% and 9% respectively.
The policy was expensive; nevertheless, it proved effective.

cards.definition: in addition to what has been said
cards.example: Furthermore, remote work reduces commuting emissions.
Urban birth rates fell; conversely, rural ones rose.
With regard to funding, opinions remain divided.
In light of these findings, the policy was revised.

cards.definition: although (used before an adjective or phrase)
cards.example: The scheme succeeded, albeit at considerable cost.

cards.definition: the total greenhouse gases produced by a person or activity
cards.example: Flying less is the quickest way to cut your carbon footprint.

cards.definition: energy from sources that are naturally replenished
cards.example: The country now generates 40% of its power from renewable energy.
Planting trees can help mitigate the effects of flooding.

cards.definition: able to continue without damaging the environment
cards.example: Sustainable farming protects soil for future generations.

cards.definition: the reduction of a resource until it runs low
cards.example: The depletion of fish stocks threatens coastal economies.
The tax is designed to reduce industrial emissions.

cards.definition: to work towards a particular profession
cards.example: She left banking to pursue a career in medicine.

cards.definition: training for a specific trade or job
cards.example: Vocational training often leads to employment faster than a degree.

cards.definition: an education covering a broad range of subjects
cards.example: A well-rounded education develops more than exam skills.

cards.definition: the pleasure someone gets from their work
cards.example: Many people value job satisfaction more highly than salary.

cards.definition: to widen your experience and understanding
cards.example: Studying abroad really broadened my horizons.

cards.definition: abilities useful in many different jobs
cards.example: Teamwork and communication are transferable skills.
I've always looked up to my grandmother.
I took up photography during the pandemic.
My French is basic, but I get by when I travel.
He comes across as shy, but he's very talkative once you know him.
I kept putting off my exam preparation until the last month.

cards.definition: to stay level with; to stay informed about
cards.example: It's hard to keep up with all the changes in technology.
